title: Chicken breast, baked, broiled, or roasted with marinade, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken breast is a lean source of protein prepared by baking, broiling, or roasting with a flavorful marinade. Cooking without the skin keeps the meat tender while reducing fat content. It is widely used in low‑fat diets, salads, quick‑cook meals, and various world cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides about 31 g of protein per 100 g, making it one of the most protein‑dense meat cuts.
Marinades often contain lemon juice, herbs, spices, and a small amount of oil, which enhance flavor and juiciness.
When baked or grilled without skin, the finished product typically contains less than 3 g of fat per 100 g.
Chicken breast is a staple in sports nutrition because of its high protein and low calorie profile.
In Hungarian cuisine, chicken breast is commonly used in "paprikash," a stew flavored with sweet paprika.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Protein is essential for muscle growth, repair, and immune function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Skinless breast contains very little saturated fat, supporting heart health.

items.title: B vitamins
items.content: It provides niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken breast supplies phosphorus, selenium, and zinc, vital for bones and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Weight‑management support
items.content: High protein and low calorie content help promote satiety and aid weight control.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor pathogens such as Salmonella. Cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Although uncommon, some individuals may be allergic to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Marinades can be high in salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you need to limit sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice cooked breast for salads, add to sandwiches, stir‑fries, rice or vegetable dishes, or serve as a main course with a side. It pairs well with lemon, garlic, herbs, and light sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw breast refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Store cooked breast in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or slimy texture.
